description_and_commentary: Despite consistently achieving higher academic success, female students at the School face barriers in transitioning to graduate employment. They face obstacles in securing graduate employment, compounded by confidence in engaging with professional networks, limited resources for portfolio development, a lack of mentorship opportunities, inadequate digital skills, and a deficit in cultural capital. aim: To reduce the gap in participation in HE for students from underrepresented groups

These milestones represent a continual year-on-year improvement in our recruitment of BAME UK undergraduates throughout the period of this plan. We give an undertaking to refine our milestones and targets before the start of 2020/21 to address the gap between specific under-represented groups within BAME and the general UK UG population. We aim to reduce the gap between BAME and non-BAME students and aim to increase the percentage of BAME students in the UK UG population. We will use our own Access and Participation monitoring dataset (drawn from our student records system and UCAS and HESA data) to record progress against this target (owing to small numbers). The baseline is set against our own absolute performance (as detailed in Table 1a of our APP).

aim: To reduce the gap in percentage points between the RVC's IMD 1 and IMD 5 cohorts
description_and_commentary: Our target is to reduce the pp gap between IMD Q1 and Q5 students at the RVC. Students from IMD Q1 are less likely to aspire to undertake a veterinary based course due to lack of early life exposure to animals, poor guidance at the school level and perceived financial barriers. It is, therefore, very ambitious for us to reduce this gap. We anticipate that as we refine our activities based upon evidence, the changes will gain momentum and thus predict narrowing the gap more in the final 3 years of the plan compared to the first two.

aim: To reduce the gap between RVC and national population in terms of BAME groups

We are cognisant that this represents a very ambitious target for the RVC as there are cultural, religious and social barriers for some BAME students aspiring to work in the Veterinary profession.

The target has been set to achieve the upper end of the benchmark position over five years.

Our participation rate for BAME LPN Q1 and Q2 student numbers have increased by 3.9% over the past 5 years. Targeting BAME specifically because this is where the biggest gap occurs. The target has been set to continue that trend of improvement.

RO wishes to demonstrate maximum ambition for RO students and track two years of access to RIUs using HEAT data. RO will therefore only be able to report on a milestone after two years, to allow for HESA data to be gathered via HEAT. For example, data for reporting on 2020-21's milestone will be available from Spring 2023.

aim: Increase the proportion of LPN Q1 students entering UoL when they are HE ready
description_and_commentary: Increase the proportion of LPN Q1 students entering UoL when they are HE ready. The University 17/18 baseline data indicates a ratio of 3.3:1, so already nearly at the OfS KPM target for 2024/25. This target proposes a raw increase in Q1 students to 14% over the period, which is above the current national participation rate of 12%. The proportions target is deemed more appropriate in this context, as a ratio or gap target could be achieved by reducing the number of Q5 students rather than increasing Q1 students, which may not be desirable.

aim: Reduce the gap in continuation between black students and white students
description_and_commentary: Black student continuation rate. Baseline black student continuation is 4% lower than white student continuation. The target has been set to close this gap to 1.5% over five years. The target is not to close the gap because the gap has widened year-on-year for the last few years, so there is a current trend to reverse also.

aim: Reduce the gap in continuation between mature students and young students

aim: To reduce the attainment gap between black and white students, year-on-year.

The target has been set to reduce the gap, recognising that interventions in this area take several years to impact. Also recognising the current trend of a widening gap needs to be reversed first. We have looked at best practice from other institutions, including the consortium project led by Kingston University to support academic leadership at a programme level to enable inclusive curriculum enhancements and improve outcomes for students from BAME backgrounds.

The Brilliant Club supports pupils from under-represented backgrounds to progress to highly-selective universities. The Scholars Programme aims to improve pupils' written communication, subject knowledge and critical thinking. The academic progress of pupils who have worked with a University researcher will be assessed by comparing the baseline assignment at the beginning and a final assignment at the end of the programme, both pitched a key stage above the pupils current year group.

aim: To reduce the unexplained attainment gap between white students and black students

The difference of 11.6% in 2017/18 is not statistically significant and is based on a small population of 175 black students. We will eliminate the unexplained gap thereby reducing the difference to 5.8% by 2024/25. We expect to consolidate recent progress and develop provision, enabling us to achieve significant reductions 2022 onwards as projects deliver further impact.

aim: To reduce the gap in participation in HE for students from the most deprived backgrounds
description_and_commentary: Reduce the gap between IMD1&2 and IMD4&5 new entrants. Lincoln aspires to be more representative and give greater access to applicants from deprived backgrounds. OfS Access and Participation dataset show Lincoln's access gap for IMD1&2 new entrants to IMD4&5 new entrants is -22.2%. The gap seen at sector level is -15.1%. Lincoln aspires to be more representative and give greater access to applicants from deprived backgrounds. Our target is therefore to meet the current sector gap of 15.1% between IMD1&2 and IMD4&5 new entrants over period of the Access and Participation Plan

aim: To reduce the gap in participation in HE for students from BAME Backgrounds
description_and_commentary: Increase the percentage of new entrants from BAME Backgrounds. Lincoln aspires to be more representative and give greater access to applicants from BAME backgrounds. We do, however, recognise that our University is to some extent a reflection of a locality - the 2011 census showed that only 2.4% of the population in Lincolnshire was non-white; 3.4% of 18 and 19 year olds. OfS APP dataset shows Lincoln's BAME new entrant rate gaps to the UK population are statistically significant (-5.2% Asian, -1.8% black, -0.6% other). Our proportion of new 18 yr old entrants from BAME backgrounds is 8.3% (UK 16.1%, Sector 27.3%). Our target is to meet the combined EMids, East of England and Yorks and Humber 14.3% rate of 18 year olds from BAME backgrounds (ONS Population 2017 Estimates), over a longer ten year period. We believe this is still a stretching target.

aim: To reduce the attainment gap for students from the most deprived backgrounds
description_and_commentary: Reduce the percentage difference in degree attainment rates (1st and 2:1) between IMD quintile 5 and quintile 1 students. OfS APP dataset show Lincoln's attainment gap for IMD1 students compared to IMD5 students is -13.1%. This is statistically significant. The sector gap is -16.0%. Lincoln aspires to eliminate the degree attainment gap for students from the most and least deprived backgrounds. Taking a lead from the OfS KPM4 Success measure, by 2030/31 Lincoln aims to eliminate the absolute gap in degree outcomes between IMD1 and IMD5 students. Our target setting follows this trajectory.

aim: To reduce the attainment gap for students from BAME backgrounds
description_and_commentary: Reduce the percentage difference in degree attainment rates (1st and 2:1) between White and BAME students. OfS APP dataset shows Lincoln's attainment gap for BAME students compared to White students is -11.8%. This was previously statistically significant in 2016/17. The sector gap is -13.2%. Lincoln aspires to eliminate the degree attainment gap for students from the BAME backgrounds. Taking our lead from the OfS KPM4 Success measure, by 2024/25 Lincoln aims to eliminate the absolute gap in degree outcomes between BAME and White students. Our target setting follows this trajectory.

aim: To reduce the attainment gap for disabled students
description_and_commentary: Reduce the percentage difference in degree attainment rates (1st and 2:1) between Non Disabled and Disabled students. OfS Access and Participation dataset shows Lincoln's attainment gap for non-disabled students compared to disabled students is 4.2%. This is not statistically significant. The sector gap is 2.8%. Lincoln aspires to eliminate this degree attainment gap. Taking our lead from the OfS KPM5 Success measure, by 2024/25 Lincoln aims to eliminate the absolute gap in degree outcomes between disabled and non disabled students. Our target setting follows this trajectory.

aim: To reduce the progression to graduate employment or further study gap for Disabled Students
description_and_commentary: Reduce the percentage difference in graduate employment or further study rates between non disabled and disabled students. OfS APP dataset shows that although Lincoln's Graduate Employment or Further Study rates are higher than the sector for disabled and non disabled students, the gap is wider. The gap between non disabled and disabled students is -7.3%. The sector gap is -1.8%. Lincoln aspires to eliminate this progression gap. Taking our lead from the OfS KPM4 Success measure, by 2030/31 Lincoln aims to eliminate the absolute gap. Our target setting follows this trajectory.

aim: To reduce the progression to graduate employment or further study gap for Care Leavers

Lincoln aspires to eliminate this progression gap. Taking our lead from the OfS KPM4 Success measure, by 2030/31 Lincoln aims to eliminate the absolute gap. aim: Our aim is to reduce the gap (ratio) in participation between young full time undergraduate entrants from POLAR4 Q3-5 and Q1.

The level of ambition in our target refelcts the competitive local environments in which our campuses are located, and the fact that the year from which the baseline data is drawn follows a period of expansion for the Group with the opening of campuses in HE cold spots.

aim: To reduce the gap in participation in HE for students from underrepresented groups. Specifically to increase the proportion of disabled entrants.
description_and_commentary: Our aim is to increase the proportion of disabled full-time, first degree entrants to be at least in line or above the sector position (based on the recent sector average position of 14% in 2015/16, 2016/17 and 2017/18). Our target by 2024/25 is to increase the proportion to 1 percentage point above the current sector average proportion. The baseline is taken from the Coventry University Group 2017/18 proportion of full-time first degree entrants who had a known disability.

aim: To support access to HE for care leavers.
description_and_commentary: Our target is to support care leavers meeting the eligibility criteria linked to our new financial support package. As of January 2019 we have identified 6 students at Coventry campus whose status has been confirmed as a result of introducing a bursary in association with Santander in 2018/19. Our target is supported by the introduction of a new bursary in the form of subsidised university accommodation from academic year 2020/21. The trajectory reflects an aim of recruiting 10+ care leavers per year and continuing to support them for the duration of their course.

aim: To support the National KPM 4 to eliminate the unexplained attainment gap for students from underrepresented groups: specifically between Black students and White students.
description_and_commentary: To decrease and eliminate the unexplained gap - Percentage difference in degree attainment (1st and 2:1) between White students and Black students by 2024/25. Measured by an increase in the value added score for Black students. This is a foundation for reducing overall attainment gaps. The baseline data uses a value added score for 2016/17. (Kingston method). An increased value added score indicates a reduced gap between the actual proportion of students awarded a 1st or 2:1 compared to the expected proportion taking factors such as entry qualifications and subject of study into account. A score of 1 or above indicates that students have been awarded a classification at a level that would be expected given their prior attainment and subject of study.

aim: To maintain a value added score of 1 or above for Asian students during the period 2024/25, as a foundation for reducing overall attainment gap for Asian students by 2030/31.
description_and_commentary: To maintain a value added score of 1 or above for Asian students during the period 2024/25, as a foundation for reducing overall attainment gap for Asian students. The baseline data uses a value added score for 2016/17 for Asian students. (Kingston method). A score of 1 or above indicates that students have been awarded a classification at a level that would be expected given their prior attainment and subject of study.

aim: To support the National KPM 5 to eliminate the attainment gap between disabled students and nondisabled students by 2024/25.

aim: To support the National KPM 4 to eliminate the absolute attainment gap for students from underrepresented groups: specifically between Black students and White students.

aim: To reduce the gap in progression to employment or further study between BAME and white FT first degree graduates
description_and_commentary: Our aim is to reduce the absolute percentage point gap in rates into employment or further study between our BAME and White qualifiers. Our target by 2024/25 is to reduce and halve the gap between BAME and White qualifiers from over 8 percentage points (baseline taken from 2016/17) to just over 4 percentage points, to a level that is below the current sector level gap. Our progression rates for both BAME and White graduates are strong and above sector level. We will seek an alternative measure with the introduction of the Graduate Outcomes survey which will be published in 2020.

aim: Aim for an increase proportion in access from POLAR Quintile 1.
description_and_commentary: The College will target an increase in access from Quintile 1 by 2% for 2020/21 with longer-term strategies towards the ambition to further improve this, reaching 30% by 2025. The College has already strengthened our investment in schools' liaison activity (through the newly recruited Schools Marketing Executive and extended contracts for NCOP staff). The College's longer-term strategy is to increase access from Quintile 1 to 30% by 20-25.

aim: Address the decline in the continuation rates of Quintile 1 (by increasing the continuation rate of IMD 1 Q1 students).
description_and_commentary: Increase continuation rates for IMD Q1 students year-on-year reaching 80% in 2024/25. We have an aim to close the continuation rate for Q1 students across a five-year period in order to raise this back to the figures pre-LCCA collaboration in 2015-16 (85%). With no more LCCA activity post January 2020 and due to the specific low continuation rates for this collaborative delivery, we anticipate that continuation will rise dramatically across the duration of the plan.

aim: BAME - close the continuation gap between white and asian students.
description_and_commentary: Close the continuation gap (20%) between white and asian students, reaching just 2% in 2024/25. The number of asian students that attend Walsall College (both Campuses) increased in 2017/18, when the College began collaborated delivery with LCCA (due to the demographic of LCCA's location (Central London). College has recorded that continuation for LCCA students remains an area for improvement.

aim: BAME - close the continuation gap between white and black students.
description_and_commentary: Close the continuation gap (38%) between white and black students, reaching just 5% in 2024/25. The number of black students that attend Walsall College (both Campuses) significantly increased in 2017/18, when the College began collaborated delivery with LCCA (due to the demographic of LCCA's location (Central London). College has recorded that continuation for LCCA students remains an area for improvement.

aim: Mature continuation (reduce gap). Reduce continuation gap between mature and young students.
description_and_commentary: Reduce the 9% gap in continuation rates for our mature students across the five-year plan, reaching 0% in 2024/25. The increase in student numbers, following commencement of the partnership with LCCA, has altered the percentage of student continuation. In order to close the gap, the College must explore opportunities for changes, such as timetable flexibility to ensure that the continuation of older students increases.

aim: Diabled continuation (reduce gap). Target to reduce the continuation gap between disabled students and students with no known disability.
description_and_commentary: Reduce the 12% continuation gap between disabled students and students with no known disability across the five year plan, reaching 0% in 2024/25. The continuation rates for students that are not known to be disabled in 2017/18 was 61% (an increase of 8%). The disability gap in continuation rate for can be attributed to low numbers of students with a disability (which disproportionally magnifies the comparison) however, the actual decline in the continuation of those declaring a disability cannot be overlooked in this same way and therefore will appear as a targeted area for improvising across the five-year length of this plan.

aim: Learning Difficulty continuation (increase proportion). There is a small minority of students with multiple learning difficulties where continuation rates were not as high as their peers.
description_and_commentary: Maintain and review continuation rates termly throughout 2021. This will remain an area to monitor for retention to improve by 2% across the five-year plan. Whilst there is no longer any material gap for those with dyslexia, the statistics show a small minority of students with multiple learning difficulties performed less well and therefore remain an area to monitor and improve continuation.

aim: IMD Progression (increase proportion). There is clear disparity between progression rates of IMD students from Q1 in 2016/17 compared to other HE providers.
description_and_commentary: Address the disparity between progression rates of IMD students from Q1 compared to other HE providers, improving progression by 23% over the five-year plan. Quintile 1 progression has improved by 19%, but remains significantly lower than the national average and therefore a stronger data set will allow scrutiny at course level to explore preparation for next steps. Actions to improve this across 5 years resulting in parity with national averages for all cohorts.

aim: Mature Progression (increase proportion). There is a clear disparity between the college progressions of mature students compared to their younger counterparts in 2018/19 compared to other HE providers.
description_and_commentary: Address the disparity between the college progression rates of mature students compared to young people improving progression by 20% over the five-year plan. Whilst progression for mature students has improved by 20% since 2015/16, and is 12% above young people, it is still 20.7% below that of other providers nationally and therefore requires improvement.

aim: To increase the proportion of young male students entering from low participation neighbourhoods
description_and_commentary: Proportion of young (18/19 year old) males recruited to UCR provision from low-participation neighbourhoods (POLAR4 quintiles 1 and 2). 34.7% (25 - 17/18) of the male student population (108 - 17/18) at UCR originate from low-participation neighbourhoods. To address this issue, we must diversify our curriculum to provide a more broad range of provision. A steady-state for the first three years is therefore proposed to enable curriculum developments and robust marketing to impact on LPN male recruitment. Our ambition is to recruit at least 40% of our male cohort from LPN's by 2024/25.

Strategies will focus on further establishing a more inclusive environment for learning, teaching and assessment and embracing the social model of disability, with close observation of relevant monitoring groups assoicated with disability.

aim: To inspire and enable more people from areas of lower socio-economic income and low participation to embark on a journey to success in life through higher education at HCA in creative subjects.
description_and_commentary: Increase the proportion of enrolments for POLAR Q1 & Q2 to the institution. Recruiting from this hard to reach group into a specialist College of Arts, neccessitates a long lead time. We have not marked them as collaborative targets as the baseline data is HCA's but we will work within our NCOP to align/amplify work. The targets are the guide to the trend, but the trajectory and overall target will be the key judgement points, rather than an isolated year's performance.

aim: To increase the ethnic diversity of our student population and ensure they have an equal and as excellent experience and outcomes as other students
description_and_commentary: Increase the proportion of BAME enrolments to the institution. We have not targeted this group of students before, and so have no data from our activity to drive accurate target setting. The number of students is very low, leading to data volatility. Whilst we have put numerical targets by year, in reality, the targets will be taken as a trend over a number of years. We expect school and college relationship building to payback over an extended period, rather than in the short term. The actual number of students will increase with HCA's projected growth.

aim: To increase the proportion of the mature student population and ensure they have an equal and as excellent experience and outcomes as other students
description_and_commentary: To increase the proportion of the mature student population. HCA has a relatively large proportion of mature students, but a declining trend. We will reverse this trend whilst maintaining a balanced student body.

aim: To close the gap in the continuation between POLAR Q1&2 students POLAR Q3,4&5 students.
description_and_commentary: We aim to close the gap in continuation for students from POLAR Q1&2 when compared to Q3,4&5. This has been volatile data, which reflects the low numbers of students. The targets are the guide to the trend, but the trajectory and overall target will be the key judgement points, rather than an isolated year's performance. Actual rate 85% Cont Q1&2. Cont rate Q3,4,5 =93%. This differs frrom the APP Dataset gaps report.

comparator_group: Students not in receipt of DSA
aim: To close the gap in the attainment between disabled students and non disabled students.
description_and_commentary: We aim to close the gap in attainment for students in receipt of DSA when compared with students not in receipt of DSA. This is based on internal college data. Although the baseline percentage gap is small, it is significant given the level of support these students recieve and as yet our incomplete data for 2018-19 indicates a downward trend that needs to addressed.

aim: To decrease gaps in continuation for some mature students
description_and_commentary: Decrease the gap in continuation between young and mature students. The College will work to decrease this gap with particular focus on older mature students where internal data indicates a larger contination gap compared with youg students.

aim: To close the gap in the attainment between POLAR Q1&2 students POLAR Q3,4&5 students.
description_and_commentary: We aim to close the gap in attainment for students from POLAR Q1&2 when compared to Q3,4&5. Recent internal data (2017-18) shows that students from Q1 achieved better than students from Q2; Q1 Attainment- 69%, Q2 Attainment68%. Aggregated Q1&2 Attainment- 69%. Aggregated Q3,4,5 Attainment75%.

aim: To increase the progression rate for disabled students.
description_and_commentary: We aim to increase the proportion of disabled students progressing to higher level employment or further study. Because our progression data is inconsistent we have opted to target overall progression rather than closing a gap to an unstable overall performance. We have a long term objective to support the development of Higher Level employment in Herefordshire. This is beyond the scope of the college and relies on many strategic partnerships across the county. Beyond 5 years we will close the gap on the wider sector.

comparator_group: Wider 18 year old population from IMD Q1
aim: By 2025, to have developed access and admissions activity and academic provision that is as attractive and accessible to those in the most deprived areas in our region as it is to others, so that those individuals can reach their full educational potential. Closing the equality of access gap between the most economically disadvantaged applicants (IMD 1) and their peers is our first target aim.
description_and_commentary: Percentage point gap for access between full-time 18 year olds from IMD Q1 joining the institution and the wider 18 year old population from IMD Q1. Current baseline refers to specific under-representation by 14 percentage points for full-time 18-year old entrants from IMD Q1 relative to the wider population of 18 year olds from IMD Q1, and then how that gap will close over the period.

comparator_group: Wider population of Asian and Black 18 year olds
aim: By 2025, to have created as accessible, representative and nourishing a learning community for BAME applicants seeking a personal, pastoral, scholarly, supportive, aspirational and nonurban tertiary academic experience as for other learners. Closing the equality of access gap between Asian/Black 18 year olds and their peers is our second target aim.
description_and_commentary: The percentage point gap for access between full-time Asian 18 year old intake compared to the wider population of Asian 18 year olds is joint weakest in the UK; The full-time Black 18 year old intake gap compared to the wider population of Black 18 year olds is smaller, but still poor in sector terms. The challenge is to encourage more Asian and Black applicants to apply to the University, and for more of those applicants, having received an offer, to choose University of Chichester. Data is combined percentage point gap for Asian and Black 18 year old entrants data compared to wider 18 year old population, with disaggregation in the APP document.

aim: By 2025, to have built a diverse and inclusive context, culture and curriculum through which all BAME students are able to achieve their full attainment potential. Closing the equality of attainment gap between all BAME students and their peers is our third target aim.
description_and_commentary: Our BAME attainment gap is 12 percentage points, just under sector mid-point of 13.2. Our BAME numbers are relatively small, so this measure is volatile. Actions include dispelling BAME deficit myths; listening to and involving BAME students; ensuring equal entitlement to use of support services, resources and opportunities; developing an inclusive curriculum framework appropriate to our context and culture. May need to recalibrate interim targets during period, but to set any less stretching target is unjustifiable. Given this steep challenge we have built in outer end years acceleration to incremental and final targets.

aim: By 2025, a) To have better understood and more effectively implemented approaches to social/educational mobility, motivation and transition to study, and models of supported work/study that significantly enhance attainment and life chances for economically disadvantaged Males in our region. Closing the equality of attainment gap between economically disadvantaged Male students (IMD 1/2) and IMD 1/2 Females is our fourth target aim.
description_and_commentary: Our 19 percentage point gap for economically disadvantaged Male students' attainment compared to Female students with the same background is the worst of our benchmark group and is one of the worst in the sector (currently 3.8). Given our starting position, it is considered too stretching to close the gap entirely within the first five years of action. Clearly, should improvement accelerate our incremental targets will be appropriately recalibrated during the period.

aim: To reduce the 3.2% access gap for WWCM at Bradford compared to the sector to 1% by 2024/25
description_and_commentary: Proportion of new entrants where sex = male, IMD quintile = 1, and ethnicity = white, out of those where these characteristics are known. Applies to full-time and apprenticeship undergraduates. The University has a very small proportion of 'white working class males' despite a significant population within its key recruitment areas. The University is therefore setting an ambitious target to significantly increase these numbers. Some collaborative work will be undertaken with NCOP to achieve this target, in addition to the University's own outreach activities as detailed in the APP.

aim: To significantly reduce the 40.8% access gap between care leavers and the general population to 10.8% by 2024/25.
description_and_commentary: Data on care leavers is collected for submission to the HESA Student Return. Applies to full-time and apprenticeship undergraduates. Care leavers are under-represented nationally and numbers in Bradford are increasing. 12% of care leavers enter HE nationally compared to 49.8% for the general population. We have used the population of care leavers in Bradford as a proxy to assess our performance at care leaver access. Based on this our performance equates to 9%, a 40.8% gap. We are seeking to improve from 9% to 30%, reducing the gap to10.8% overall. Data sources are our SRS and data from our local authority.

aim: To eliminate the 10.7% attainment (proportion of good honours) gap between BAME and white students to 0%, by the end of the milestone period.
description_and_commentary: Percentage difference in good honours graduates between white and BAME students. Applies to full-time and apprenticeship undergraduates. Multiple initiatives are in place to address this, as detailed in the narrative submission. The gap has already gone down from 17.0% in 2013/4 to 10.7% in 2017/8. Breakdown of BAME groups has been undertaken - there has been significant improvement in attainment for black students, however the University is concerned to sustain this over a longer period, and to undertake further work to address the gaps for other BAME groups.
